title: Etale normal forms for a nodal family with etale markings
statement: Let $X,Y$ be locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], $(Y,T)$ a log regular pair with divisorial log structure $M_Y$ [def-trf-log-regular-pair], and $f:X\to Y$ flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty connected one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Suppose $f$ is smooth over $Y\setminus T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, meaning its ideal is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], etale over $Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and supported in the relative smooth locus. At every geometric point $x$ over $y$, after taking etale neighbourhoods $U\to X$ and $V\to Y$, with $U\to V$ over $f$, the following normal forms are available. At a smooth unmarked point one may arrange $D\cap U=\varnothing$ and $U\to V$ smooth. At a marked point there is an etale $V$-morphism $U\to\mathbf A^1_V$ with coordinate $z$ for which $D\cap U$ is exactly $z=0$. At a nonsmooth point one may arrange $D\cap U=\varnothing$ and an etale $V$-morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}_V(\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h))$, sending the chosen point to $u=v=0$, where $h\in\mathcal O_V$ is a function invertible on $V\setminus T_V$, $T_V=V\times_Y T$. Consequently $h$ is a section of $M_Y|_V$, and after a further etale refinement there is a fine saturated chart $c:P\to M_Y|_V$ and an expression $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$, with $\varepsilon\in\mathcal O_V^\times$, $a\in P$, and $\alpha:P\to\mathcal O_V$ the chart structure map. All these neighbourhoods may be refined to carry a fine saturated chart of the base.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71, equation (1.a) and the smooth-locus case. The marked coordinate is the smooth relative curve coordinate adapted to the etale Cartier marking.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point x of X over y in Y and work after shrinking etale neighbourhoods around x and y. If x is smooth for f and x is outside D, the relative smooth locus is open and D is closed, so choose U and V with x in U, U→V smooth, and U disjoint from D. This gives the smooth unmarked normal form. The hypotheses used here are exactly flatness, local finite presentation and the stated nodal fibres (which make the smooth locus the complement of the nodal points). The fitting-singular lemma asks for equidimensional geometric fibres of dimension one: a connected one-dimensional Noetherian fibre has no zero-dimensional irreducible component, since such a component would be a clopen point or would lie in another component; so the stated fibre condition gives it, together with the assumption that f is smooth away from T.

source.place: Tag 0CBY setup and the smooth-locus case; ILO Exposé VI, Proposition 1.9, pp. 70–71.

proof.text: Suppose instead that x lies on D. Since D is supported in the relative smooth locus, f is smooth at x; after shrinking U and V, both U→V and the closed immersion D×_XU→U are smooth over V, the latter because D→Y is etale. Apply the etale-coordinate theorem for a smooth closed pair [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates]. At x the relative dimensions are one for U→V and zero for D×_XU→V, so its integers are a=0 and b=1. Therefore the resulting etale V-map is U→A^1_V, with one coordinate z, and the inverse image of the coordinate subspace is exactly D×_XU; hence D∩U is z=0.

source.place: Exposé VI, Proposition 1.9, smooth-locus/marked case, pp. 70–71.

proof.text: Finally let x be nonsmooth. Apply the etale local model of an at-worst-nodal family [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] (Stacks Tag 0CBY) at the image point of x; its hypotheses are flatness, local finite presentation and the nodal geometric fibres, equidimensional of dimension one as in step 1. It supplies etale U→X and V→Y, U→V over f, h∈Γ(V,O_V), and an etale V-map U→W=Spec_V(O_V[u,v]/(uv−h)) with a point of U over x; since U→X is etale the residue extension at that point is finite separable, so the geometric point x lifts to U. U→X×_YV is etale (a morphism between etale X-schemes), and smoothness of a morphism at a point is unchanged by etale maps on the source and by the etale base change V→Y; hence a point of U is nonsmooth for U→V exactly when its image in X is nonsmooth for f, and exactly when its image in W is nonsmooth for W→V. On the fibre κ(v)[u,v]/(uv−h(v)) of W the Jacobian (v,u) vanishes only at u=v=0 and only when h(v)=0, so the lift of x goes to the node locus u=v=0 and h(y_V)=0. Because D is contained in the relative smooth locus, shrink U so that D∩U is empty. The singular locus is the complement of the relative smooth locus by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular]. Let N⊂W be the node locus u=v=0, which maps isomorphically to V(h). The image of U is open and contains the chosen node, so its intersection with N is an open neighbourhood of the image point in V(h); its complement Z in N≅V(h) is closed in V, and we replace V by V∖Z and U by its inverse image. Any h=0 point v' of V outside T_V then has its node point in the image of U, hence a nonsmooth point of U over v', whose image in X is a nonsmooth point of f over a point of Y∖T, contradicting smoothness over Y∖T. Hence h has no zero on V∖T_V, i.e. it is invertible there. This is precisely the equation uv=h in Tag 0CBY; no projectivity assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family and its proof; the smoothness-away-from-T assertion is the smooth-locus hypothesis in ILO Exposé VI, Proposition 1.9.

proof.text: At the same time refine V etale-locally so that the divisorial log structure M_Y has a fine saturated chart c:P→M_Y; this is available from the definition of a fine saturated log-regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. On the nodal chart, h is invertible over V\T_V, hence h is a section of M_Y by the definition M_Y=O_Y∩j_*O_{Y\T}^×. The chart description of a fine saturated log structure says that every such section is a chart element times a unit, so h=εα(a) for some a∈P and ε∈O_V^×. Refining the smooth and marked neighbourhoods over the same V gives the asserted common fine saturated base chart.

source.place: Exposé VI, Proposition 1.9 and §§1.4, 1.8, pp. 69–71; divisorial-chart factorization.
